transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess what finally scared me into coming in is my work. I'm a camera operator and video editor, and I just... I keep making these really dumb technical mistakes that I absolutely know better than to make. 

Like, I'll end up labeling camera cards wrong, or I'll completely miss a timecode note. Or I'll export a client cut with the wrong lower-third graphic on the screen, even after I've actually sat there and checked it. It's just becoming a real problem, and I need to figure out what's going on.
Have you had this kind of trouble with attention to detail and careless mistakes since you were a child?

Yeah, it definitely goes back to when I was a kid. Um... even in elementary school, my teachers were constantly having to move my desk away from other kids. I was just always out of my seat, or blurting out answers, or... bothering my classmates before I even really realized I was doing it. So, yeah, it's been an issue for a long time.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks or conversations?

Um, no, not really. I don't think so. I can usually stay focused on a conversation or a task just fine. Like, if I'm cutting a video, I'm fully in it... it's just that I'll make those careless mistakes while I'm working, or I'll rush through it. But I don't really find myself drifting off or losing my attention entirely. So, no, I wouldn't say that's a big issue for me.
Do you often have trouble waiting your turn?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I have a hard time waiting in lines or anything like that. I guess I can get a little impatient sometimes, but I wouldn't say it's a major problem for me. It's not something that stands out.
As an adult, do you still often feel restless or fidgety?

Yeah, I definitely do. Um... for example, sitting still through a client screening feels like there's this pressure building under my skin. I just feel like I need to get up and do something with my body, even when I know I'm supposed to just sit there and watch quietly. So, yeah, I still deal with that a lot.
As an adult, do you often interrupt other people or blurt things out before they’ve finished speaking?

Yes, I do that quite a bit. Um, I tend to jump in with answers before the director or a client has even finished their question. I just hear the first few words and react right away. And then... sometimes halfway through my response, I realize I'm answering the completely wrong thing because I didn't actually wait to hear the rest of what they were asking.
